topic: Why octopuses have three hearts but can die of a broken one
narration: Three hearts should make you unkillable. That's the assumption about octopuses: built-in backup pumps, pure redundancy. In reality, two hearts only serve the gills, and the main one stops beating every time it swims. Their blood runs on copper, which carries oxygen poorly, so the body needs constant high pressure; swimming overloads the main heart, and it stalls. After she lays eggs, a gland floods her with self-destruct hormones; she stops eating, and her heart slowly quits. Three hearts, and she still dies of a broken one.
